[#hash-digests-choose]
.How to choose among "Digests"
[cols="2,2,2,4,4",options="header"]
|===
| Name | Fastest natively | Smallest on Emscripten | Where it is used | Choose it when

| <<hash-legacy,`md5_128`>>
| 933 MiB/s (hash2)
| 8,039 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6151[legacy checksums and old protocols; RFC 6151 retires it for signatures]
| Only to read or check data that already uses it.

| <<hash-legacy,`sha1_160`>>
| 1,190 MiB/s (hash2)
| 10,285 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://git-scm.com/docs/hash-function-transition[Git's original object ids, with collision detection]; link:https://shattered.io/[the first public collision, SHAttered (2017)]; link:https://sha-mbles.github.io/[the first public chosen-prefix collision, SHA-1 is a Shambles (2020)]
| Only to read or check data that already uses it.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_224`>>
| 606 MiB/s (hash2)
| 14,116 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's shorter SHA-2]
| When a standard asks for it; otherwise SHA-256.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_256`>>
| 593 MiB/s (hash2)
| 14,108 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf[Bitcoin's block and transaction ids (twice)]; link:https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md[Nostr's event ids (NIP-01)]; link:https://git-scm.com/docs/hash-function-transition[Git's SHA-256 object format]; link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#appendix-B.4[TLS 1.3's cipher suites]
| The default digest: interoperable everywhere, in every browser, fast with hardware support.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_384`>>
| 913 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,579 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#appendix-B.4[TLS 1.3's AES-256 cipher suite]
| When a standard asks for 192-bit strength, or a digest that resists length extension within SHA-2.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512`>>
| 940 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,582 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8032#section-5.1[Ed25519's signatures]; link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039.mediawiki[BIP39's seeds, through PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512]
| When a standard asks for it, or for a 512-bit digest.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512_224`>>
| 941 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,645 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's truncated SHA-512]
| When a standard asks for it.

| <<hash-sha2,`sha2_512_256`>>
| 911 MiB/s (hash2)
| 17,597 bytes (hash2)
| link:https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4[FIPS 180-4's truncated SHA-512]
| A 256-bit SHA-2 digest that resists length extension, fast on 64-bit machines.

| <<hash-digest-family,`digests::md5`>>
| -
| -
| link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6151[legacy checksums and old protocols; RFC 6151 retires it for signatures]
| To name the backend in the call, or to hash in pieces with a result that cannot be taken twice; md5_128 itself for hash_append and Boost.Hash2's other functions.

| -
| -
| link:https://git-scm.com/docs/hash-function-transition[Git's original object ids, with collision detection]; link:https://shattered.io/[the first public collision, SHAttered (2017)]; link:https://sha-mbles.github.io/[the first public chosen-prefix collision, SHA-1 is a Shambles (2020)]

The measured columns are doc/measurements.json's, a reference measured on 2026-11-16 on Apple M5 Max that decides nothing: the native throughput over 1 MiB, or the time of one derivation over `hmac_sha2_256`, of the fastest backend, and the smallest Emscripten program that calls the function; <<hash-measurements>> has every backend on every target.
